usage: Modifier form: 정확한 정보 'accurate information', 정확한 시간 'the exact time'.
Polite present. 하다 verbs drop 하 and add 해요.
Both adverb forms are common; 정확히 sounds slightly more written.
Negative; often used as 정확하지 않아요 to soften 'that's wrong'.
examples: 이 번역이 정확한지 한번 확인해 주세요.
Please check once whether this translation is accurate.
정확한지: 정확하다 + -ㄴ지 'whether it is ~'.
시간을 정확히 지켜 주셔서 감사합니다.
Thank you for keeping the time exactly.
정확히 + 지키다 = 'keep precisely / be punctual'.
제 기억이 정확하다면 회의는 3시였어요.
If my memory is accurate, the meeting was at 3.
정확하다면: -다면 'if (it is the case that)'.
nuance: 정확하다 is about matching the truth or a standard with no error — accurate numbers, correct facts, precise timing. It overlaps with 맞다 ('be right') but is more formal and emphasizes precision rather than just being acceptable. Use it for data, translations, pronunciation, and measurements.
mistakes: Do not confuse with 확실하다 ('be certain/sure'); 정확하다 is about correctness, 확실하다 is about confidence/certainty.
Avoid '정확하다 정보' — use the modifier form 정확한 정보.

usage: 자세한 설명 'a detailed explanation', 자세한 내용 'detailed content'.
Polite present, though the adverb 자세히 is used far more often.
The go-to adverb form: 자세히 설명하다 'explain in detail'.
Common request phrase in conversation and email.
examples: 이 부분을 좀 더 자세히 설명해 주시겠어요?
Could you explain this part in a bit more detail?
자세히 + 설명하다 is a fixed collocation.
자세한 일정은 메일로 보내 드리겠습니다.
I'll send the detailed schedule by email.
자세한 + noun, formal written register.
계약서를 자세히 읽어 보고 사인하세요.
Read the contract carefully before you sign.
Here 자세히 means 'closely, thoroughly'.
nuance: 자세하다 describes something that includes a lot of specific detail, and its adverb 자세히 also means doing something closely/thoroughly (reading, looking). In speech you will hear 자세히 (adverb) much more than the plain adjective. It is the natural word for asking someone to elaborate.
mistakes: The adverb is 자세히 (with ㅣ), not 자세하게 in most everyday phrases — both exist, but 자세히 is far more idiomatic.
Don't use it to mean 'careful' in the sense of caution; that is 조심하다.

usage: 적절한 표현 'an appropriate expression', 적절한 대응 'an appropriate response'.
Polite present; common in feedback and evaluations.
examples: 그 상황에서는 그 말이 적절하지 않았어요.
In that situation, those words weren't appropriate.
Past negative: 적절하지 않았어요.
문제에 적절한 해결책을 찾고 있습니다.
We are looking for an appropriate solution to the problem.
적절한 + noun, formal.
가격이 적절해서 바로 계약했어요.
The price was reasonable, so I signed right away.
Here 적절하다 implies 'fitting / reasonable'.
nuance: 적절하다 means well-suited to the situation, context, or purpose — the 'right' choice given the circumstances. It is more formal and judgment-oriented than 맞다, and is common in writing, work, and evaluations (e.g., an appropriate word, response, or measure). It carries a sense of social/contextual fit.
mistakes: 적절하다 vs 적당하다: 적절하다 = 'fitting/apt for the context'; 적당하다 = 'a moderate/just-right amount or degree' (and can be casual). They are not always interchangeable.
Use 적절한 (modifier) before a noun, not 적절하다.

english: to be moderate, just right, adequate
usage: 적당한 운동 'moderate exercise', 적당한 크기 'a suitable size'.
Polite present; very common in everyday speech.
Adverb: 적당히 하다 'do something in moderation / not overdo it'.
give it a rest / don't overdo it
Casual idiom telling someone to stop going too far.
examples: 국이 너무 짜지 않고 간이 적당해요.
The soup isn't too salty; the seasoning is just right.
적당하다 of taste/amount = 'just right'.
주말에는 적당히 쉬고 적당히 일해요.
On weekends I rest a moderate amount and work a moderate amount.
Repeated 적당히 = 'in good balance'.
이 정도 가격이면 적당한 것 같아요.
I think this price is reasonable.
적당한 것 같다 = 'seems just right'.
nuance: 적당하다 expresses a comfortable middle — not too much, not too little, neither extreme. It is more casual and quantity/degree-focused than 적절하다. The adverb 적당히 can be positive ('in moderation') or carry a slightly negative 'just enough to get by / half-heartedly' nuance depending on context and tone.
mistakes: 적당히 can imply doing something carelessly or half-heartedly ('적당히 했어' = 'I just did it roughly'); read the tone before assuming it's positive.
Don't swap with 적절하다 in formal evaluations — 적절하다 sounds more proper there.

usage: 충분한 시간 'enough time', 충분한 준비 'sufficient preparation'.
Adverb already in the app as a separate word; here as a derived form: 충분히 이해해요 'I fully understand'.
Softer than 부족하다 for saying 'that's not quite enough'.
examples: 준비할 시간이 충분하니까 천천히 하세요.
There's enough time to prepare, so take your time.
충분하니까: -니까 'since/because'.
이 정도면 두 명이 먹기에 충분해요.
This much is enough for two people to eat.
-기에 충분하다 = 'enough to ~'.
네 마음은 충분히 이해해.
I fully understand how you feel.
충분히 as an intensifying adverb = 'fully, well enough'.
nuance: 충분하다 means a quantity, time, or degree reaches or exceeds what is needed. It is the natural opposite of 부족하다. The adverb 충분히 is extremely useful and often means 'fully/plenty' rather than just 'enough' (e.g., 충분히 가능해요 'it's totally possible'). It works for tangible amounts and abstract things like understanding or rest.
mistakes: Don't say '충분 있어요'; 충분하다 is an adjective, so use 충분해요 or 충분한 N.
충분하다 vs 풍부하다: 충분하다 = 'enough for the need'; 풍부하다 = 'abundant/rich', emphasizing plentifulness beyond mere sufficiency.

english: to be lacking, insufficient, short of
usage: 부족한 부분 'the lacking part', 부족한 점 'shortcomings'.
잠이 부족하다 'be short on sleep', 경험이 부족하다 'lack experience'.
Set humble phrase: 부족하지만 잘 부탁드립니다.
examples: 요즘 잠이 부족해서 너무 피곤해요.
I've been short on sleep lately, so I'm really tired.
잠이 부족하다 is a fixed collocation.
아직 경험이 부족해서 더 배우고 싶어요.
I still lack experience, so I want to learn more.
경험이 부족하다 = 'lack experience'.
부족한 점이 많지만 열심히 하겠습니다.
I have many shortcomings, but I'll work hard.
부족한 점 = 'shortcomings', humble register.
nuance: 부족하다 is the direct opposite of 충분하다 and marks the thing in short supply with 이/가 (잠이 부족하다, 돈이 부족하다). Beyond literal shortages it is also a humble, polite way to describe one's own abilities or work ('부족하지만…'). Korean speakers use this self-deprecating 부족하다 frequently to sound modest.
mistakes: Mark the short item with 이/가, not 을/를: 시간이 부족해요 (not 시간을 부족해요).
Don't confuse with 모자라다 (very similar meaning but more colloquial, and can also rudely mean 'dim-witted' about a person).

usage: 풍부한 경험 'rich experience', 풍부한 자원 'abundant resources'.
Adverb: 영양이 풍부하게 들어 있다 'richly contains nutrients'.
examples: 이 과일에는 비타민이 풍부해요.
This fruit is rich in vitamins.
비타민이 풍부하다 is a common health phrase.
그분은 경험이 풍부해서 믿음이 가요.
She has rich experience, so I trust her.
경험이 풍부하다 = 'experienced'.
감정 표현이 풍부한 배우예요.
She's an actor with rich emotional expression.
풍부한 + noun, descriptive register.
nuance: 풍부하다 emphasizes plentiful abundance — more than enough, generously full. It is common with experience, resources, nutrients, emotions, and knowledge. Compared with 충분하다 ('enough for the need'), 풍부하다 highlights that there is a lot, often as a positive quality. It tends to appear in slightly more formal or descriptive contexts.
mistakes: Mark the abundant thing with 이/가: 자원이 풍부하다 (not 자원을 풍부하다).
Don't use 풍부하다 for a person's body shape; for 'plump' use 통통하다 instead.

usage: 독특한 디자인 'a unique design', 독특한 맛 'a distinctive taste'.
Adverb: 독특하게 꾸미다 'decorate in a distinctive way'.
About a person it can hint at 'eccentric'; tone matters.
examples: 이 카페는 분위기가 정말 독특해요.
This cafe has a really distinctive atmosphere.
분위기가 독특하다 = 'unique vibe'.
향이 독특해서 호불호가 갈릴 것 같아요.
The scent is distinctive, so opinions will probably be divided.
독특해서: -아/어서 'because'.
그 사람은 생각이 좀 독특한 편이에요.
That person's way of thinking is a bit unusual.
About a person, 독특하다 can mean 'quirky'.
nuance: 독특하다 describes something noticeably different from the ordinary — distinctive, original, one-of-a-kind. For food, design, or style it is usually positive ('unique, characterful'). Applied to a person's personality or ideas it can lean toward 'quirky/eccentric', so tone and context decide whether it's praise or a gentle warning.
mistakes: 독특하다 vs 특별하다: 독특하다 = 'distinctive/unlike others'; 특별하다 = 'special/significant'. Unique is not always 'special'.
Calling a person 독특하다 can sound like a polite way of saying 'odd', so use it carefully.

english: to be effective, produce good results
usage: ~적이다 adjectives take 적인 before a noun: 효과적인 방법 'an effective method'.
examples: 단어를 외울 때는 이 방법이 가장 효과적이에요.
When memorizing words, this method is the most effective.
Predicate use: 효과적이에요.
시간을 효과적으로 쓰는 법을 배우고 싶어요.
I want to learn how to use time effectively.
효과적으로 = adverb '~적으로'.
광고가 효과적이어서 매출이 늘었어요.
The ad was effective, so sales went up.
효과적이어서: ~적이다 + -아/어서.
nuance: 효과적이다 means something actually works well and produces the intended result — effective. It is a ~적이다 adjective, so remember the patterns: 효과적인 N (modifier), 효과적이에요 (predicate), 효과적으로 (adverb). It is closely related to 효율적이다, but focuses on whether the desired effect is achieved at all, not on resource economy.
mistakes: Don't drop 이: it's 효과적이다 / 효과적이에요, not '효과적다'.
Before a noun use 효과적인, and as an adverb use 효과적으로 — mixing these up is a very common error.

english: to be efficient (good output for the input)
usage: 효율적인 동선 'an efficient route/flow', 효율적인 일 처리 'efficient handling of work'.
Adverb: 시간을 효율적으로 관리하다 'manage time efficiently'.
Prefix 비- negates it: 비효율적인 방식 'an inefficient way'.
examples: 이렇게 하면 일을 더 효율적으로 할 수 있어요.
If you do it this way, you can work more efficiently.
효율적으로 + 하다, very common at work.
우리 팀은 회의를 효율적으로 진행해요.
Our team runs meetings efficiently.
회의를 효율적으로 진행하다 = 'run meetings efficiently'.
에너지를 효율적으로 쓰는 가전을 샀어요.
I bought an appliance that uses energy efficiently.
효율적으로 쓰다 = 'use efficiently'.
nuance: 효율적이다 is about getting the most result with the least time, effort, or resources — efficiency. It pairs naturally with work, time management, and energy use. The key contrast with 효과적이다: 효과적이다 asks 'does it work?', while 효율적이다 asks 'is it worth the input?'. Something can be effective but not efficient, and vice versa.
mistakes: Keep the patterns straight: 효율적인 N, 효율적이에요, 효율적으로 (adverb).
Don't use it as a synonym for 효과적이다 — efficiency (cost) and effectiveness (result) are different ideas.

english: to be clear, distinct, vivid, marked
usage: 뚜렷한 목표 'a clear goal', 뚜렷한 차이 'a distinct difference'.
Both adverbs exist; 뚜렷하게 is more common in speech.
Near-synonym of 모호하다 when describing vague impressions.
examples: 한국은 사계절이 뚜렷한 나라예요.
Korea is a country with four distinct seasons.
사계절이 뚜렷하다 is a classic textbook phrase.
두 제품의 차이가 아주 뚜렷해요.
The difference between the two products is very clear.
차이가 뚜렷하다 = 'a marked difference'.
그는 자기 의견이 뚜렷한 사람이에요.
He is a person with clear-cut opinions.
의견이 뚜렷하다 = 'has firm, well-defined views'.
nuance: 뚜렷하다 means something stands out clearly and is well-defined — distinct seasons, a sharp difference, a firm opinion, a vivid memory. It overlaps with 분명하다 and 명확하다 but leans toward 'visibly distinct / sharply outlined' rather than 'logically certain'. It is the natural opposite of 모호하다 and 흐릿하다.
mistakes: Mark the distinct thing with 이/가: 차이가 뚜렷하다 (not 차이를 뚜렷하다).
Don't use 뚜렷하다 to mean 'certain that something is true' — for that, prefer 확실하다 or 분명하다.

usage: 명확한 기준 'clear criteria', 명확한 답변 'a clear answer'.
Polite present; common in work and academic contexts.
명확하게 밝히다 'state explicitly'; 명확히 is slightly more formal.
명확하지 않은 부분 'the part that isn't clear'.
examples: 규정을 좀 더 명확하게 설명해 주세요.
Please explain the rules a bit more clearly.
명확하게 설명하다 = 'explain explicitly'.
책임 소재가 명확하지 않아서 문제가 생겼어요.
It wasn't clear who was responsible, so a problem arose.
명확하지 않다 = 'ambiguous, unclear'.
목표를 명확히 세우는 것이 중요해요.
It's important to set your goals clearly.
명확히 세우다 = 'set clearly/definitively'.
nuance: 명확하다 means clearly defined and free of ambiguity — explicit criteria, unambiguous answers, well-defined responsibilities. It is more formal/written than 분명하다 and is preferred in work, rules, and academic writing. It is the natural opposite of 모호하다, emphasizing that nothing is left vague or open to interpretation.
mistakes: 명확하다 (clear/unambiguous) vs 정확하다 (accurate/correct): clarity is not the same as correctness.
Use the modifier 명확한 before a noun, and 명확하게/명확히 as the adverb.

usage: 모호한 태도 'an ambiguous attitude', 모호한 표현 'a vague expression'.
Emphatic compound; very common in speech.
examples: 대답이 너무 모호해서 무슨 뜻인지 모르겠어요.
The answer is so vague that I can't tell what it means.
모호해서: -아/어서 'because'.
기준이 모호하면 사람마다 다르게 이해해요.
If the criteria are vague, each person understands them differently.
기준이 모호하다 = 'unclear standards'.
그는 태도가 모호해서 속을 알 수 없어요.
His attitude is ambiguous, so I can't read his true feelings.
태도가 모호하다 = 'noncommittal attitude'.
nuance: 모호하다 is the opposite of 명확하다/뚜렷하다 — blurry, unclear, open to multiple interpretations. It applies to language, criteria, attitudes, and boundaries. In daily speech you'll often hear the stronger compound 애매하다 or 애매모호하다 for 'wishy-washy / hard to pin down'. It frequently carries a mildly negative tone of frustration that something isn't clear.
mistakes: In casual speech 애매하다 is more common than 모호하다 for 'iffy/unclear'; 모호하다 sounds a touch more formal/written.
Don't confuse with 헷갈리다 ('to be confused/mixed up'), which describes the listener's confusion, not the thing's vagueness.
